Shadowfin: New Danish Ultra-Low-Cost Underwater Drone. Few countries are contributing as much as Denmark to Ukraine’s defence. A 7-meter (23 ft) underwater drone exhibited at the DALO Industry Days 2026 in Denmark on 19th-20th August is of particular interest. Unlike most new AUV (autonomous underwater vehicle) designs it is unambiguously low cost (around €50k) and geared to the expendable nature of modern drone warfare. This purposeful design is expected to be arriving in Ukraine later this year. 

 

 The Shadowfin drone is designed and built by Danish company Søens Tech , which has a background in innovative Mechatronics technologies to support underwater infrastructure projects, especially in Horizontal Directional Drilling (HDD). The Shadowfin is thus, while innovative and unconventional, developed by engineers intimately acquainted with watery arena. 

 Among Western designs Shadowfin stands out as being engineered for truly low-cost warfare. Its hull is a simple fiberglass tube, and the thrusters are commercial off the shelf units. While this will limited its operating depth, it results in a very affordable platform. 

 
 Shadowfin on display at DALO Industry Day 2026. Photo Naval News . 

 Specifications (estimates)

Length: 7 meters

Diameter: ~0.5 m

Displacement: 1.5 tons

Payload: ~300 kg
 

 The thrusters are unusual. Shadowfin uses two rim-drive pumpjets where the blades rotate around the outside of the rim, leaving the center where the axel normally is completely clear. This arrangement is increasingly available in commercial thrusters, but has yet to be widely seen in defence projects. 

 The rim-drive pumpjets appear to be an underwater-optimised type built by Copenhagen Subsea . Rim drive designs use the rim itself as the motor, eliminating the need for the complexity and moving parts of the hub. Passing electricity through the rim spins the ring directly, removing the need for a gearbox, drive shaft, or seals. This means that it should, in general, be quieter too. 

 
 Shadowfin on display at DALO Industry Day 2026. Photo Naval News . 

 The design features a tall, fixed mast which can house cameras and other sensors, as well as navigation and communications antenna. It is also proposed that it could include a short mast to allow an internal combustion engine in the hull, which would significantly increase endurance. 

 Shadowfin is intended to carry a 300kg payload, about the same as a heavyweight torpedo, enabling both ISR (intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance) missions and direct strike. Soens Tech propose an improved version, Shadowfin Enhanced , armed with a MU90 Impact lightweight torpedo. This weapon is not used by Denmark but has been sold to Ukraine for use aboard their future Ada Class corvettes. Soens intend it to provide an anti-submarine warfare capability. У Канаді вироблятимуть НРК TerMIT для України та країн НАТО

Українська компанія TENCORE та канадська Dominion Dynamics запустять виробництво НРК TerMIT у Канаді для потреб України та партнерів НАТО.

Про це у компанії TENCORE розповіли Мілітарному.

У межах міжнародної оборонної виставки AUSA 2026 українська компанія TENCORE та канадська Dominion Dynamics підписали меморандум про взаєморозуміння.

Партнерство української та канадської компанії, окрім локалізації, передбачає також інтеграцію канадської системи автономного керування та навігації AuraNet.

У межах партнерства TENCORE забезпечить трансфер технологій та навчання канадських фахівців для виходу на серійне виробництво.

Зі свого боку, Dominion Dynamics інтегрує власний софтверно-апаратний комплекс командного керування та автономії AuraNet, а також розробить спеціалізовану модифікацію TerMIT для роботи в екстремальних арктичних умовах.

Передача НРК TerMIT Фото: Tencore

Випуск перших серійних зразків канадського виробництва заплановано на 2027 рік.

«Партнерство з Канадою дає нам масштабовану виробничу базу, стійкі ланцюги постачання та надійну енергосистему, щоб запускати цей цикл разом із союзниками, яким потрібні перевірені рішення», — зазначає співзасновник TENCORE Роман Ткаченко.

Базова версія НРК НРК TerMIT створена для транспортування вантажів із запасом ходу до 40 км, швидкістю до 15 км/год та балістичним захистом для стабільної роботи під час логістичних місій.

Також є версії TerMIT з бойовим модулем «Хижак» виробництва UGV Robotics.

У червні стало відомо, що також у Німеччині вироблятимуть НРК для України на спільному підприємстві Quantum Systems і Tencore.

ВМС Греції випробували морські дрони Corsair, які США використовували проти Ірану

Про це повідомляє профільне видання Naval News з посиланням на заяви Міністерства оборони Греції.

Міністр оборони Греції Нікос Дендіас під час заходу заявив про прагнення країни стати європейським лідером у сфері розробки та застосування автономних платформ до 2030 року.

russia Tests 15kg Jet Interceptor Drone DF-1 Roscherk at 500km/h While Developing 850km/h DF-3 Gadyuka Based on Italian Fighter Shape

russian company DOFA-Tek during DronCongress 2026 forum first announced development of its new jet air-defense drone DF-1 Roscherk, designed for intercepting jet unmanned aerial vehicles.

Quite impressive characteristics were announced for new DF-1 Roscherk. Specifically, declared maximum range is up to 250 km, flight duration up to 50 minutes, maximum speed up to 500 km/h, cruising speed up to 400 km/h, or in economy flight mode up to 200 km/h.

Despite such large range of entire 250 km, DF-1 Roscherk has mass of only 15 kg, of which warhead can account for up to 1.5 kg. Additionally, construction of this air-defense drone is all-metal, which according to developers will simplify production.

DF-1 Roscherk is launched from guide rails using solid-fuel rocket booster, which provides acceleration and brings drone to required altitude and speed. Details regarding guidance and communications system have not been announced yet.

As of now DF-1 Roscherk is at factory testing stage, with next public tests planned for November this year. Meaning DF-1 Roscherk is no longer just project, but working solution that may soon pose obstacle to Ukrainian long-range unmanned aerial vehicles.

Besides DF-1 Roscherk, rashists are developing other jet drones as well. Specifically this concerns more powerful air-defense drone DF-3 Gadyuka and long-range strike unmanned aerial vehicle DF-5 Iskra. Most interesting among them is DF-3 Gadyuka.

For DF-3 Gadyuka, maximum range of entire 800 km is declared. It has cruising speed of 650 km/h, and also maximum speed up to 850 km/h, which may be sufficient for intercepting some cruise missiles.

At same time, DF-3 Gadyuka mass compared to DF-1 Roscherk increased significantly, now standing at gigantic for air-defense drone 240 kg. Meaning in size and range this is almost deep strike, but designed for intercepting drones, and here one can recall Ukrainian jet long-range drone Bars, which was converted into interceptor.

Interestingly on sole published image of DF-3 Gadyuka, it has shape suspiciously similar to Italian light fighter-bomber Aeritalia G.91. Meaning rashists could have simply taken successful aerodynamic design of that aircraft as basis for their drone.

Regarding DF-5 Iskra, following characteristics are declared: maximum range up to 1,200 km, speed 850 km/h, and also takeoff mass of 120 kg, of which warhead accounts for 20 kg.

However both DF-3 Gadyuka and DF-5 Iskra, unlike DF-1 Roscherk, judging by everything are currently only at early development stages. Therefore they appear to be still far from serial examples and factory testing.

Ukraine’s hobbit-named robot fired on targets up to 1.3 km away in a demo for border guards

Ukraine’s six-wheeled Frodo ground robot fired on targets during a demonstration in Kharkiv Oblast for the Pomsta (Revenge) Border Guard Brigade, a border guard detachment posted on Facebook. Frodo made its public debut only on 30 September.

Ukraine had contracted more than 22,000 ground robots for 2026 by July, mostly logistics carriers, with combat models the smallest group, the Defense Ministry said. Frodo’s first reported mission was an evacuation. The demo shows its armed version to a fighting brigade, the kind of robot Ukraine has ordered least.

The platform completed its tasks at a training ground in near-combat conditions, said the 3rd Border Guard Detachment named after Hero of Ukraine Colonel Yevhenii Pikus. The Buria turret mounted on Frodo can fire either a Mk 19 automatic grenade launcher or a Browning M2 heavy machine gun. It engaged targets at up to 1.3 km (0.8 mile), the detachment said.

The 47-kg (104-lb) module has a ballistic calculator, stores up to 256 targets, aims in three seconds, and has a stated autonomous run time of up to 48 hours, the post said. Frodo is rated for up to 150 km (93 miles) on paved roads and 75–80 km (47–50 miles) over rough terrain, the post added. A Frontline Robotics Zoom reconnaissance drone flew reconnaissance during the test.

The developer, Frontline Robotics, describes its core philosophy as arriving fast, doing the job, and leaving very fast—hit and run, the detachment’s post said. Familiarizing the brigade’s soldiers with such systems aims first and foremost to preserve personnel’s lives and health, the detachment said.

Frontline Robotics told Militarnyi at the unveiling that Frodo had passed Defense Ministry codification and was built for logistics, evacuation, and strike missions. The robot reaches 40 km/h (25 mph) and carries up to 200 kg (441 lb) of payload, or 400 kg (882 lb) at most, the company said. A single soldier can swap its batteries.

The 92nd Assault Brigade used an early test unit to evacuate a wounded soldier, Frontline Robotics told Militarnyi. An operator, callsign Tango, named the robot’s speed and its ability to handle complex maneuvers as its main advantages, Militarnyi reported.

Зв’язок зникає після 161 км/год: Starlink обмежив перехоплення «Герань-4», «Герань-5» і «Бандероль» реактивними дронами-перехоплювачами

Обмеження швидкості роботи Starlink на території України зберігаються — це перешкоджає використанню супутникових терміналів у дронах-перехоплювачах реактивних «Шахедів».

Про це президент України Володимир Зеленський повідомив в аудіоповідомленні журналістам.

За словами президента, Україна веде діалог щодо роботи Starlink і Starshield на рівні військових, Міністерства оборони та дипломатів. Українська сторона намагається зв’язатися з усіма причетними, зокрема з компанією SpaceX. Однак наразі компанія не відповідає українським військовим і Міністерству оборони, тоді як на різних рівнях американці пояснюють ситуацію «технічними проблемами».

Президент наголосив, що проблеми виникають лише на території України: після перевищення швидкості 161 км/год приблизно на другій хвилині зв’язок повністю зникає, що призводить до втрати дронів. Водночас у країнах Європейського Союзу цих проблем немає, що українська сторона вже перевірила.

«Ми відправили пару машин на території країн Європейського Союзу зі Starlink, і вони їхали зі швидкістю, там, де це можна, зі швидкістю 180 км/год плюс, і Starlink працює. У нас є відповідні фіксації, є відповідні докази. Висновок наступний: обмеження діють на території України, і обмеження не діють на території країн Європейського Союзу. Тобто це спланована операція», — наголосив він.

Такі обмеження унеможливлюють застосування оснащених Starlink дронів-перехоплювачів проти реактивних «Шахедів» та інших швидкісних безпілотників. Тому для протидії цим загрозам Сили оборони вимушені продовжувати використовувати авіацію, ракети та інші засоби ППО.

Загалом, за словами президента, українська авіація збиває близько 55–60% реактивних «Шахедів». Водночас це створює значне навантаження на українські винищувачі, які мають значний строк експлуатації, та на обмежену кількість пілотів.

Зокрема, близько половини винищувачів F-16 тривалий час перебувають у Європі на ремонті та технічному обслуговуванні. Проблеми з обслуговуванням цих літаків пов’язані, зокрема, з тим, що деякі компоненти для ранніх модифікацій F-16 більше не виробляють, а закуповувати їх дедалі складніше.

Для вирішення цієї проблеми країни-партнери України працюють над прискоренням ремонту українських F-16. Так, бельгійська компанія Sabena Engineering, яка відповідає за технічне обслуговування українських винищувачів, щомісяця ремонтує чотири F-16 й планує невдовзі збільшити обсяги обслуговування до шести літаків на місяць.

Наразі публічно повідомлено про декілька моделей дронів, які використовують для перехоплення реактивних «Шахедів»: P1-SUN JetKiller, SPYS, Sting S та перехоплювач, імовірно, створений на основі ракети-дрона «Барс». При цьому перші три є подальшим розвитком електричних квадрокоптерів, тоді як дрон-перехоплювач «Барс», імовірно, оснащений реактивним двигуном.

The Tyr is 790 mm long, and is fitted with swept wings with a 1,000 mm wingspan, batteries being located in the wings. Its mass at launch is 2.3 kg; for infantry use a reusable ground launcher is available. This comes in the form of a nearly rectangular box capable to contain the Tyr, the impulse is given by a crossbow-like mechanism, the propeller being activated as soon as the airframe leaves the launcher. The solution adopted allows to reuse it several times. “The mass of the overall system including munition, radio link, ground control station and launcher is around 6.8 kg. When the wings are disassembled from the fuselage the system can be fitted in a rucksack, one man being able to carry more than one munition within a reasonable load,” Mr. Haagenrud told EDR On-Line.

Once airborne the Tyr navigates towards the target area via waypoints using GNSS signals, however the munition is fitted with a much smarter navigation system which exploits the images provided by four sensors, a day camera and a thermal imager located at the front and two similar sensors installed under the fuselage, as well as information provided by magnetometer and gyroscopes; all those information are fused and allow to minimise the drift of the inertial navigation system which is used in GNSS-denied areas. Although such a solution requires a considerable amount of computing power, EDR On-Line understood that today on the civilian market very powerful processors are available at a reasonable price. The computing power is also used to fuse the images provided by the four cameras. “When doing so we obtain what might be defined a ‘virtual gimbal’, saving mass and money. Not only, we can zoom-in on an object while keeping all the peripheral view,” Nils-Andreas Haagenrud explained.

The Tyr flies autonomously to the target area. At this point it starts loitering, searching for a target, and when it identifies one it warns the operator. “We have an automatic target recognition on board. To fully understand what is needed to recognise a target and to lock onto it, and how far away from the target we can lock onto it so to avoid losing the radio link, I have personally been several times to Ukraine in the last four year,” the company President told us. At this point the automatic tracking system locks on the target and the Tyr starts diving on it. Not before having received the green light for the attack from the operator, who sends the signal that arms the warhead. “Right now, considering western countries legal issues, we have the man in the loop, it is him the one that presses the button and engages the target. However, the Tyr can be used as a fire-and-forget munition, should a government decide that this is acceptable,” we were told, a solution that would obviously be better used against static targets rather than against armoured vehicles.

The dive angle will depend very much on the type of target; EDR On-Line understood that the munition can go from a horizontal hit to a vertical one, top attacks at different angles being the preferred options against many types of targets, static and on the move. Typically it is easier to destroy a main battle tank hitting the top of the turret or the powerpack at the rear, something which is done at high angles of attack. Soft target in the open may be dealt with overflying the area, therefore flying a much more flat path.

Considering the Tyr lethality package, in August 2026 Heaviside Industries inked a partnership with Nammo of Norway, the latter becoming its warhead supplier for multi-domain precision munitions platforms, of which Tyr is the first example. Four different types of warheads are made available: shaped charge, against tanks and armoured vehicles; explosively formed penetrator, also against heavy armoured targets; fragmentation, against light armoured targets and personnel in the open; enhanced blast, against protected structures.

“The beauty with NAMMO is that they can tailor these warheads as we want them, the Tyr having a maximum payload of around 700 grams, although we are trying to use as much off-the-shelf payloads as possible. For example, the shaped charge solution is was developed by NAMMO together with the Norwegian armed forces, it is a very capable system and we are testing it right now. The three other warheads are now undergoing initial testing,” Mr. Haagenrud said. Depending on the type of target and warhead, not only the angle of attack must be optimised, but also the distance from target at which the warhead detonates. In the front section of the Tyr we find three windows, two of them hiding the day and the thermal cameras, the third hiding a laser rangefinder. “It gives you the information on how far you are from the target, which in case of a shaped charge warhead will allow to detonate it at the optimised stand-off distance, usually well under one metre, while in case of the fragmentation warhead you may want to detonate it from 3-4 metres all the way up to 20-30 metres, depending on the type of target and the fragment density you want to obtain,” the Heaviside Industries co-founder detailed. EDR On-Line understood that in the final dive, especially at high angles, the munition accelerates mostly under the effect of the force of gravity, reaching a speed limit of over 250 km/h.

Until now we mentioned only the use from the ground. The company has already done tests dropping the Tyr from helicopters and light aircraft, and some more will be carried out soon. The use from mid-size UAVs is also conceivable as well as that from naval platforms, in the latter case using a similar launch system to the one used from the ground.

Heaviside Industries Tyr has completed live-firing tests, and is currently under contract with US Department of War customers.

“We are in low rate initial production right now. We are testing and making sure we get away with all the teething problems. We know that it takes time to get the system up to the level where it becomes extremely reliable, because this is the most important thing,” Nils-Andreas Haagenrud stated.

A loitering munition in the class of the Tyr is destined to be produced in great numbers.

For airborne platforms, every pound matters. More weight requires more energy to lift, which requires more batteries, which add more weight. This quickly becomes a vicious circle. If you can put more energy into the same battery weight, you meaningfully change that math. Greater energy density batteries become enablers of greater range, endurance, and mission capability. Lithium-ion technology has been extraordinarily successful, and will remain the right choice for many applications, but it is reaching its entitlement performance. The different chemistries and ways of putting those together deliver different combinations of energy, power, cycle life, safety, and cost.

For applications where weight and endurance are especially important, lithium-metal anode batteries are compelling because replacing the graphite anode with lithium metal reduces weight and volume, and increases energy density. Those gains significantly enhance mission capability.

Sion Power has been at the forefront of lithium-metal battery innovation for more than 25 years. Over the last 15 years, we’ve developed robust IP around high-energy density batteries for electric vehicles. At our Tucson facility, we have approximately 2,000 test channels and a 5,300-square-foot safety and abuse lab dedicated to rigorous performance and safety testing – from exposure to extreme temperatures and vibration, to nail penetration, and forced discharge.

We understand that our batteries need to perform reliably in diverse environments and conditions, and we are constantly expanding the capabilities on that front. (defense customers will be using our batteries in non-hostile environments as well)

Bradley’s Old TOW Launchers Get New Teeth With Spike Missile Adapter

Rafael USA and Leonardo DRS have presented a capability that would allow fighting vehicles equipped with legacy Tube-launched, Optically tracked, Wire-guided (TOW) missile launchers to fire Rafael’s Spike LR2 anti-armor missiles. The effort builds on a demonstration dating back to 2021, with the companies now presenting a more mature adapter solution designed to integrate the Israeli-made missile into existing platforms.

Roman Palaria, Rafael’s vice president for marketing and business development in its land and naval division, discussed the system in an interview with TWZ at the Association of the U.S. Army’s (AUSA) main annual convention. He explained that the earlier demonstration, part of Project Convergence 2021, used a version of the adapter that had not yet reached its final configuration. Leonardo DRS, Rafael’s U.S. partner, subsequently developed the mechanical and electrical components needed to connect the Spike LR2 to the TOW launcher and the vehicle’s existing systems.

The approach is intended to avoid replacing the launcher or radically overhauling the vehicle’s gunner station. Instead, the adapter provides the mechanical interface for loading the Spike LR2 missile and the electrical connections needed to communicate with the vehicle. Additional electronic components are installed within the vehicle to support the missile’s functions.

“We’re doing minimum changes to the vehicle,” Palaria said, describing the goal of making the integration as seamless as possible for the operator.

The Bradley infantry fighting vehicle is a prominent potential application, although the companies say the capability could extend to other platforms that use TOW launchers. The Army has operated TOW-equipped vehicles for decades, creating a substantial installed base of launch systems that could potentially benefit from the approach. As for the Bradley, the Army effort to replace its TOW missiles has been a long one, but is yet to produce any real results.

Spike LR2 was successfully test-fired from M2A4 Bradley equipped with Multi-Purpose Missile Launcher (MPML), developed by Rafael and DRS. Adapters allow the system to remain compatible with existing TML/UTML launchers. Spike LR2 has also been proposed for the CCMS-H and XM30. pic.twitter.com/KB9EYwi6BI

After a missile is fired, its launch tube remains in the launcher and can be removed to accommodate another missile.

The central attraction of the system is the ability to combine existing launcher infrastructure with the Spike LR2’s unique engagement capabilities.

During Project Convergence 2021, two Spike missiles were fired from a TOW launcher, and both reportedly hit their intended targets. The adapter now being presented reflects subsequent development work by Leonardo DRS, including refinement of the mechanical interface and vehicle electrical integration.

The system is designed to preserve the vehicle’s existing TOW capability while adding the option to use Spike LR2. That would give commanders another missile option without necessarily requiring wholesale replacement of installed launcher equipment. The extent to which individual vehicles could use both missile types would depend on the completed integration and applicable qualification requirements.

The Spike LR2 offers capabilities differ substantially from those of the legacy TOW missile. Palaria cited a maximum range of approximately 5.5 kilometers (3.4 miles) and highlighted the missile’s day/night imaging seeker, which provides video to the operator during flight. The longest-range TOW missile versions max out at around 4.5 kilometers (2.8 miles).

RAFAEL's Spike LR2 Missile

In contrast, Spike LR2’s imaging capability supports engagement of targets beyond the operator’s direct line of sight, as well as observation of the target area during the missile’s approach. Depending on the engagement, the operator can acquire a target through the missile’s seeker, adjust the engagement, or select a different target while the missile is in flight.

These features contrast with the traditional TOW’s semi-automatic command to line-of-sight (SACLOS) guidance, in which the gunner tracks the target through the launcher’s observation system and guides the missile throughout its flight. Spike LR2’s onboard imaging provides a different set of options for engagements in which direct observation is limited or target conditions change after launch. This can also include striking targets behind cover.

Palaria also described the LR2’s two warhead options. The first of these is a tandem-charge anti-tank warhead, which Rafael claims is able to penetrate any modern main battle tank. It consists of a precursor warhead and the main warhead, which are designed to penetrate the reactive armor, and the main armor, respectively.

Rafael's SPIKE LR2 HEAT IMPACT

The second option is a multi-purpose configuration. It has a programmable fuze, which allows the missile to be employed against different target types. Depending on the selected mode, the warhead can be configured for direct-impact or timed-detonation effects, for example, detonating above the ground for anti-personnel missions, or penetrating a building, in which case the first charge will make a hole in in a wall, and then the second charge will go inside and explode after a short delay.

The adapter offers a potential route to adding new missile capabilities to existing Army vehicles while limiting changes to their launcher hardware and crew interface.

Operator training would obviously be necessary. Although the gunner would continue using the vehicle’s existing console and displays, Palaria acknowledged that Spike LR2 introduces additional functions, controls, and engagement procedures.

For the Army, the proposition is straightforward: retain a familiar launcher architecture while potentially adding a missile with greater reach, onboard imaging, and more flexible engagement options that exceed line-of-sight tracking. The adapter’s significance lies in making that combination possible without starting from a clean sheet.

Whether that capability becomes a fielded upgrade will depend on the Army’s requirements, testing, integration decisions, and procurement plans. But the widespread uptake of the Spike series of missiles around the globe, combined with the very large existing TOW missile operator base, means the adapter solution could well be of interest to customers outside the U.S. Army, too.

Shadowfin: New Danish Ultra-Low-Cost Underwater Drone. Few countries are contributing as much as Denmark to Ukraine’s defence. A 7-meter (23 ft) underwater drone exhibited at the DALO Industry Days 2026 in Denmark on 19th-20th August is of particular interest. Unlike most new AUV (autonomous underwater vehicle) designs it is unambiguously low cost (around €50k) and geared to the expendable nature of modern drone warfare. This purposeful design is expected to be arriving in Ukraine later this year. 

 

 The Shadowfin drone is designed and built by Danish company Søens Tech , which has a background in innovative Mechatronics technologies to support underwater infrastructure projects, especially in Horizontal Directional Drilling (HDD). The Shadowfin is thus, while innovative and unconventional, developed by engineers intimately acquainted with watery arena. 

 Among Western designs Shadowfin stands out as being engineered for truly low-cost warfare. Its hull is a simple fiberglass tube, and the thrusters are commercial off the shelf units. While this will limited its operating depth, it results in a very affordable platform. 

 
 Shadowfin on display at DALO Industry Day 2026. Photo Naval News . 

 Specifications (estimates)

Length: 7 meters

Diameter: ~0.5 m

Displacement: 1.5 tons

Payload: ~300 kg
 

 The thrusters are unusual. Shadowfin uses two rim-drive pumpjets where the blades rotate around the outside of the rim, leaving the center where the axel normally is completely clear. This arrangement is increasingly available in commercial thrusters, but has yet to be widely seen in defence projects. 

 The rim-drive pumpjets appear to be an underwater-optimised type built by Copenhagen Subsea . Rim drive designs use the rim itself as the motor, eliminating the need for the complexity and moving parts of the hub. Passing electricity through the rim spins the ring directly, removing the need for a gearbox, drive shaft, or seals. This means that it should, in general, be quieter too.

Ukraine races to field faster interceptors as Russia hammers its energy grid

KYIV, Ukraine — Russia is still using fast jet-powered drones to batter Ukraine’s energy facilities, bridges and other critical infrastructure at speeds beyond the reach of most of Kyiv’s drone interceptors, despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s unilateral announcement on Sunday of an energy ceasefire between the two countries.

Russia began using the jets heavily in July, when their numbers jumped fivefold from the previous month. They can now reach speeds of up to 373 mph (600 km/h) — more than three times the speed of the propeller-driven Geran-2 drones they evolved from — far exceeding the top velocity of the average Ukrainian interceptor drone, air force officials told lawmakers last week.

To stop the drones, Ukraine must instead rely on F-16s, newly installed machine gun turrets that use artificial intelligence to aim and costly air-defense missiles that are in short supply globally.

“Ukraine did not strike Russian oil refining and the energy sector in general for two days after the American president announced a ceasefire in the energy sector. But Russia did not listen to the American president,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote after jets seriously damaged a gas production facility in the northeastern Kharkiv region on Sunday night.

Russia launched 167 missiles and drones overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, including 77 jet-powered drones, which officials said struck one of Kyiv’s main power plants and left 600,000 without power.

Ukraine’s Air Force says they are beginning to field more effective countermeasures, but with Russia continuing to optimize the design of jet-powered drones to destroy critical infrastructure, the development of jets and anti-jet interceptors has become the latest neck-and-neck technology race on the battlefield.

Iran shipped Russia its first Shahed-131 and Shahed-136 drones in mid-August 2022, and Moscow rebranded them the Geran-1 and Geran-2 and was firing them at Ukrainian civilian infrastructure by that October.

Those propeller-driven drones were slow enough for Ukraine to build an economical defense around mobile fire teams and cheap interceptor drones rather than spending scarce missiles on every Shahed, and in February the interceptors accounted for more than 70% of Shahed downings over Kyiv.

The jet-powered Gerans are outrunning that defense, and Russia has since stopped building the slower Geran-3 and ramped up production of the Geran-4, which cruises at 217 to 311 mph (350 to 500 km/h), and the missile-shaped Geran-5, which carries a 90-kilogram (198-pound) warhead, Militarnyi reported in August, citing Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, known as HUR.

“The Geran-5 flies 150km/h faster than the Geran-4, so the goal is to intercept from the front rather than the rear — a much harder problem to solve,” an engineer at a Ukrainian defense contractor told the Kyiv Independent.

And they are still getting faster, with the Air Force projecting speeds of 500 to 560 mph (800 to 900 km/h), though none have been recorded yet, its deputy commander, Col. Yurii Cherevashenko, told a parliamentary commission Oct. 6.

A Geran-4 version Russia began flying this autumn is built to take out infrastructure, navigating by a U.S.-made magnetometer and an optical system and carrying a new warhead designed to cut bridges and power line supports, HUR said in an Oct. 5 statement.

The new 88-pound (40-kilogram) warhead “was created specifically to destroy high-voltage pylons and iron bridge structures,” Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, an EW expert and adviser to Zelenskyy, wrote on Telegram Sept. 30 when Russia was first spotted using the upgrade on a jet drone.

These optimized Russian jet drones hit Kyiv’s South Bridge, which carries cars and metro trains across the Dnipro River, at least five times on Oct. 1 and 2, once exploding near a pier as a train crossed overhead, then struck the city’s North Bridge on Oct. 3, officials said.

Ukrainian interceptors stopped roughly 90% of the older propeller-driven drones, but against the jets, the interception rate has been significantly lower.

“Initially, we saw a very low interception rate in Ukraine. It then rose to more than 30%, and in recent nights it has increased to over 50%,” Matthias Lehna, vice president of German drone maker Quantum Systems, told Ukrinform last week.

Air force officials reported downing 77% of incoming jet-powered drones on Tuesday night.

Ukraine put its first jet interceptor, the Alexa Spatium, into service only on Aug. 21, and a handful of other prototypes, including Wild Hornets’ STING S and SkyFall’s P1-SUN Jetkiller, have successfully downed a small number of Geran-5s, according to officials speaking to the Kyiv Independent.

Fourteen companies are flight-testing jet interceptors with the Air Force, and three have shown promising results, but the deputy air force commander said officials don’t expect the jet interceptors to be delivered at the scale Ukraine needs until the end of November at the earliest.

Jet drones already make up approximately 40% of the drones Russia launches and the Air Force expects that share to reach up to 80% of total attacks.

CHAOS Industries has unveiled VESPID, a family of autonomous counter-drone interceptors that it plans to manufacture at an initial rate of 12,000 a year. The Los Angeles-based company says the design can cut costs by up to 90% compared with conventional solid-rocket-motor and turbojet interceptors.

The family includes the man-portable Mk 0 and the faster, more maneuverable Mk 1 for multitube launchers. Both are designed to defend against Group 1–3 unmanned aircraft and one-way attack threats.

VESPID uses an electric ducted fan and commercial off-the-shelf drone electronics. CHAOS says the interceptor weighs less than 12 pounds, launches in under five seconds and can engage targets up to 10 kilometers away in under 100 seconds.

Thrust vector control enables maneuvering against targets attempting to evade interception. The weapon destroys its target through direct impact rather than an explosive warhead.

“The United States and its allies require more than expensive, exquisite systems that take years to develop and are produced in limited quantities,” said Dr. Bo Marr, co-founder and chief technology officer of CHAOS Industries. “We need effective interceptors that can be built quickly, fielded broadly, and employed at a cost that makes sense against threats arriving at scale.”

CHAOS has not disclosed a unit price. Its manufacturing architecture is designed to support expansion to 50,000 interceptors annually as customer demand grows.

During the midcourse phase, VESPID receives guidance from CHAOS radars or an external command-and-control system. A direct-to-radar datalink narrows the area the terminal seeker must search and, according to the company, improves resistance to jamming.

The interceptor then switches to a commercial long-wave infrared seeker with AI-enabled target acquisition and guidance. CHAOS says engagement requires no operator input after launch and does not depend on GPS.

VESPID can integrate with existing sensors, command systems and launch platforms. Its connection to CHAOS’ NEXUS command-and-control system is intended to coordinate responses to drone swarms.

The family is interoperable with CHAOS’ multistatic radars, including VANQUISH PRIME systems. When paired with a CHAOS radar, the interceptor’s datalink signal also helps NEXUS distinguish it from hostile aircraft.

The Mk 0 can be assembled in under a minute without special tools. It launches vertically under electric fan power from the ground or a truck bed, with its battery and wings removed for transport.

The Mk 1 uses a tubular launcher with a pyrotechnic launch cartridge. CHAOS says a 10-round trainable launcher is available and gives an engagement velocity of 150 meters per second, or more than 300 miles per hour.

A planned version would carry more than 100 interceptors in a 20-foot ISO container. That configuration is intended for integration with uncrewed ground or surface vehicles.

CHAOS is relying on commercial components and simplified assembly to support high-volume production. The company’s stated aim is to give forces enough affordable interceptors to sustain protection against repeated drone attacks.

“Affordability and the ability to rapidly replace capability are not secondary considerations,” Marr said. “They are operational advantages.”

The company announced VESPID on October 12 and scheduled the Mk 1’s first public display aboard a Forterra MESA vehicle at AUSA 2026 in Washington. Founded in 2022, CHAOS manufactures its systems in the United States and has raised $1 billion from investors including 8VC, Accel and Valor Equity Partners.

Hanwha Highlights M38/M48 MUSV and Containerized Munitions at AUSA 2026

At AUSA 2026, Hanwha Defense USA featured a model of the M38 MUSV made in partnership with Magnet Defense, with the parent design vessel recently arriving at National Harbor just outside of Washington D.C. following previous rounds of testing at sea.

Hanwha’s Kevin Schoonover provided insight into the ongoing program, including several of Hanwha’s munitions offering destined to outfit the vessel and other platforms, alongside greater detail pertaining to the partnership with Magnet Defense. Schoonover also highlighted how the M38 is the primary testing vehicle for the class standing at 38 meters long, with future production upgrading to the larger 48 meter standard found on the M48. To this end steel has been cut for the first M48, with production coinciding with continued testing of the original M38.

Naval News previously reported on the partnership between Hanwha and Magnet Defense, primarily geared towards breaching the emerging U.S. USV market. Schoonover also detailed how Hanwha handles most of the construction on the vessel along with work regarding autonomous weapons integration, whilst Magnet Defense handles most of the autonomy in regards to navigation and the vessel’s actual operation.

Like similar sized USVs, the M38 also features the capability to carry containerized payloads related to multiple missions, including strike, reconnaissance, and electronic warfare. M38 has already demonstrated its range of 17,000 nautical miles on multiple tests, including a trip across the Pacific to American Samoa in up to conditions of Sea State 9 . This has been part of a bid to introduce the M38 to overseas markets, including those beyond the U.S.’s MUSV program and Korean operation.

Joining the M38 at Hanwha’s booth, the company showcased offerings for both containerized Multiple Launch Rocket Systems (MLRS) and containerized Vertical Launch Systems (VLS). There are a total of 4 different containerized systems on display, with two systems fitting inside of a 20 foot long shipping containers and the others using 40 foot standard shipping containers. When paired with M38, the vessel can carry up to 4 of the 20 foot long containerized munition packages, 2 of the 40 foot long options, or a combination of a pair of 20 foot containers and a singular 40 foot container

A containerized version of the Chunmoo family of MLRS systems constitutes one of the 20 foot options, utilizing the same munitions and launch mechanisms found on the truck based version. This enables carriage of 2 MLRS pods, with each pod containing up to 6 CGR-080 guided rockets, 4 CTM-MR ballistic missiles (with a range of 160km), 4 CTM-160 Anti-Ship Ballistic Missiles, 1 CTM-290 Ballistic Missile (with a range of 290km), or 1 CTM-X Ballistic Missile featuring a range of 500 kilometers.

The other containers represent Hanwha’s iterations on containerized VLS systems, with the other 20 foot container featuring a shortened K-VLS compact system, with 4 cells primarily meant for smaller surface to air missile systems such as K-SAAM. The two 40 foot options carry 4 cells of K-VLS I or 2 cells of K-VLS II respectively. The container with K-VLS I can employ Red Shark rocket launched torpedoes (K-ASROC), SSM-700K type surface to surface cruise missiles, and K-SAAM. The container with K-VLS II can utilize the larger L-SAM (intended to replace the SM-2 in Korean service), and other larger ballistic and cruise missiles.

U.S. Navy to Integrate LRASM into USAF’s B-52 Strategic Bombers

The U.S. Navy announced plans to contract Lockheed Martin to integrate AGM-158C Long-Range Anti-Ship Missiles (LRASM) on the Air Force’s B-52 strategic bomber. This is the latest development from the U.S. military this year to enhance and showcase its aerial maritime strike capabilities.

With its range and payload capacity, a B-52 Stratofortress equipped with LRASM can take off with a payload of 20 missiles. This capability, combined with the strategic bomber’s immense range, could prove crucial in a potential conflict against China.

Last Wednesday, Naval Air Systems Command released its intent to award Lockheed Martin for work to integrate LRASM with the B-52. The contract will involve associated testing, missile software updates and test asset repair.

The Air Force has already integrated the munition of which LRASM is derived from, the AGM-158 Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile (JASSM), across its bomber and fighter fleets. B-52 and B-1 fleets have extensively deployed the missile during the U.S.-Iran War, according to Pentagon media.

For its maritime strike-focused derivative, the Air Force first fielded the missile from the B-1 Lancer. In June, the service revealed that the B-2 Spirit stealth bomber can launch LRASM during a sinking exercise in the Indo-Pacific.

Capable of striking maritime targets at ranges exceeding 370 kilometers, the stealthy cruise missile is one of the most capable ship-sinking munitions in active U.S. service. The Lockheed Martin missiles were fired across at least four instances this summer at exercises around Hawaii and the Western Pacific. Washington showcased its operational capability from bombers, maritime patrol aircraft and naval fighters. Before the integration of LRASM, American air-based maritime strike missions solely relied on the Cold War-era AGM-84 Harpoon missile.

The U.S. Navy plans to field LRASM against enemy warships in a future high-low munitions mix. According to a Tailhook 2026 presentation, the stealthy long-range cruise missile and the low-cost Blackbeard High-Speed Long Range Maritime Strike Weapon will be key components for the future carrier air wing.

New Zealand orders five MH-60R Seahawk helicopters from United States to replace Seasprite fleet, with deliveries from 2030

New Zealand has signed an agreement with the United States to buy five MH-60R Seahawk maritime helicopters to replace its Kaman SH-2G Super Seasprite fleet. Deliveries will begin in 2030 under a project carrying NZ$1.648 billion in capital investment.

The Ministry of Defence announced the purchase on October 16 following approval of an intergovernmental Letter of Offer and Acceptance. The agreement includes weapons, spare parts, associated systems and supporting equipment.

Average annual operating funding will be NZ$110 million over the next 10 years. Funding has also been reserved for infrastructure design and temporary facilities at RNZAF Base Auckland in Whenuapai.

The Seahawks will support anti-surface and underwater warfare, search and rescue, and maritime counterterrorism operations. They will also transport personnel and supplies between ships and shore.

The ministry said the helicopters’ greater speed and ability to fly farther from ships would extend the surveillance range of New Zealand’s frigates. The aircraft will also strengthen the ships’ offensive and defensive capabilities and be interoperable with Australian and other partner defense forces.

Lockheed Martin subsidiary Sikorsky manufactures the MH-60R. The ministry lists its maximum speed at 333 kilometers per hour and its range at 963 kilometers.

The helicopter operates with a crew of three. In utility configuration, it can carry more than 1,500 kilograms of cargo.

The proposed weapons package included 225 APKWS-equipped 70 mm rockets and 65 AGM-114R Hellfire missiles, according to U.S. State Department information cited in the additional reporting. It also included five M240D machine guns and 20 Mk 54 Mod 0 lightweight anti-submarine torpedoes.

The ministry’s announcement confirmed the purchase of weapons but did not specify quantities. Its published specifications list Mk 54 torpedoes, Hellfire missiles, crew-served machine guns and APKWS among the MH-60R’s weapon systems.

The purchase makes New Zealand a new customer for the MH-60R program. Further investment decisions are expected to cover infrastructure, training systems and complementary uncrewed aerial systems.
